test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 21 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The flow of energy in the ecosystem is unidirectional.
The pyramid of energy is always inverted.
All ecosystems are stable in size.
In nature, only food chains exist, but not food webs.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The flow of energy in the ecosystem is unidirectional.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Energy flow in an ecosystem starts from the sun and flows to producers, then to consumers, and finally to decomposers.
 
• This energy transfer follows a linear path and does not cycle back, making it unidirectional.
 
• At each trophic level, energy is lost primarily as heat due to metabolic processes.
 
• Only about 10% of the energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next, known as the 10% law of energy transfer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trophic Levels**

 
 
• These are hierarchical levels in an ecosystem, comprising producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers, and tertiary consumers.
 
• Producers (e.g., plants) generate energy through photosynthesis.
 
• Primary consumers (herbivores) eat producers.
 
• Secondary consumers (carnivores) eat primary consumers.
 
• Tertiary consumers are top predators that eat secondary consumers.
 
 
 
• **Food Chains and Food Webs**
 
 
• A food chain is a linear sequence of organisms through which nutrients and energy pass.
 
• Food webs consist of multiple interconnected food chains, providing a more accurate depiction of energy flow in ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Pyramid of Energy**
 
 
• This ecological pyramid shows the energy content at each trophic level.
 
• It is always upright, indicating the loss of energy at each trophic level.
